docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
tofi is a python package for conducting tests on feature importance in machine learning. It is written on the basis of scikit-learn. Hence, in principle, any regressor/classifier learned by scikit-learn can be inferred by tofi.

tofi provides two types of Inferer for making inferences: CIT for conditional independence test and RIT for risk invariance test. CIT can implement the holdout randomization test (HRT; Tansey et al., 2022), residual permutation test (RPT; Huang, 2025), and conditional predictive impact (CPI; Watson & Wright, 2021). On the other hand, RIT can conduct leave-one-covariate-out (LOCO; Lei et al., 2018) and plug-in estimation (PIE; Williamson et al., 2023). In addition, tofi also constructs a Crosser class. With the help of Crosser, cross-fitting and \(p\)-value combination can be easily implemented to improve the stability and even statistical power of the CITs and RITs.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
tofi can be installed via pip:

pip install pytofi

The development version can be installed from GitHub:

pip install git+https://github.com/aipsylab/tofi.git

docs.title: Avoiding information leakage
docs.text: When learner is a Crosser, the sampler (CIT) or competitor (RIT) should be a Crosser with the same cv. If an ordinary estimator is passed instead, tofi issues a LeakageWarning: if that estimator was fitted on the full data, it has seen the test folds and the test is invalid.

docs.title: Tutorial
docs.text:
Three Jupyter notebooks are available to learn the use of tofi:

  1. Conditional Independence Tests
  2. Risk Invariance Tests
  3. Cross-Fitting and \(p\)-Value Combination

These notebooks assume that readers have experiences in using scikit-learn. The API reference is available at https://aipsylab.github.io/tofi/.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
pip install -e ".[test]"
python -m pytest        # unit, statistical and regression tests
ruff check . && ruff format --check .

The regression tests in tests/golden lock the numerical results of 48 scenarios. If a change of results is intended, regenerate them with python -m tests.golden.generate and document the change in CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: Inferers
docs.text:
Bases: Inferer

Conditional independence tests (HRT, RPT, CPI)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default learner estimator or crosser object

The fitted learner being inferred.

required sampler estimator, crosser object, or None

A fitted model of \(x_j\) given \(x_{-j}\). None means \(x_j\) is permuted marginally. If learner is a Crosser, sampler should be a Crosser with the same cv; otherwise a LeakageWarning is issued.

required removal int or str

Column index or name of \(x_j\).

required method ('HRT', 'RPT', 'CPI')

The testing procedure.

"HRT" See required

Bases: Inferer

Risk invariance tests (LOCO, PIE)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default learner estimator or crosser object

The fitted learner being inferred.

required competitor estimator or crosser object

A fitted model of \(y\) given \(x_{-j}\). If learner is a Crosser, competitor should be a Crosser with the same cv; otherwise a LeakageWarning is issued.

required removal int, str, or list

Column index(es) or name(s) of the removed feature(s).

required method ('LOCO', 'PIE')

The testing procedure. "LOCO" is the default, following the recommendation of Huang (2025); "PIE" (with double splitting) is available for comparison.

"LOCO" See required

An inferer for making statistical inference

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default learner estimator or crosser object

The (fitted) learner being inferred.

required sampler estimator or crosser object

A sampler that predicts \(x_j\) by \(x_{-j}\). When sampler is a crosser, its cross-validator (splitter) must be identical to the learner. If sampler doesn't have a sample method, the residual permutation approach will be used for resampling.

None competitor estimator or crosser object

A competitor that predicts \(y\) by \(x_{-j}\). If competitor is a crosser, its cross-validator (splitter) must be identical to the learner.

None removal int, str, or list

A label for removing \(x_j\). - When learner is trained with numpy array, removal must be column index(es) of \(x_j\). - When learner is trained with DataFrame, removal must be column name(s) of \(x_j\).

None method ('HRT', 'RPT', 'CPI', 'LOCO', 'PIE')

The method for making inference. It provides a control for implementing a specific procedure.

"HRT" loss_func {"mean_squared_error", "mean_absolute_error", 
    "zero_one_loss", "log_loss"}, default=None

The loss function for measuring the difference between \(y\) and its prediction.

- When `learner` is a regressor, `None` means
  "mean_squared_error".
- When `learner` is a classifier, `None` means
  "log_loss".
None null_dist ('resampling', 'normality', 'permutation')

The way for constructing a null distribution of test statistic.

- When `method` is "HRT", "RPT", `None` means "resampling".
- When `method` is "CPI", "LOCO" or "PIE", `None` means
  "normality".
"resampling" double_split bool

An indicator for double splitting. If applicable,

- When `method` is "LOCO", `None` means `False`
- When `method` is "PIE", `None` means `True`.

With double splitting, each test set is randomly divided into two halves; the learner's loss is evaluated on one half and the competitor's loss on the other.

None perturb_size non-negative float

The standard deviation of random error for pertubation. If applicable, None means 0.

None n_copies int

The number of copies for resampling \(x_j\) given \(x_{-j}\). If applicable,

- When `method` is "HRT", "RPT", `None` means 2000.
- When `method` is "CPI", `None` means 1.
None n_permutations int

The number of permutations. If applicable, None means 2000.

None random_state int or None

Controls the randomness of sampling, permutation, perturbation and double splitting. Independent random streams are derived from it for every split (fold) and every source of randomness. Unlike random_state in scikit-learn, RandomState is not allowed here.

None

Attributes:

Name Type Description method_, loss_func_, null_dist_, double_split_, n_copies_, n_permutations_

The settings actually used, i.e., the corresponding arguments with None replaced by their defaults. The arguments themselves are kept unchanged.

l_losses_ list of ndarray

Per-observation losses of learner, one array per split.

r_losses_ list of ndarray

Per-observation losses after removing \(x_j\) (resampled \(x_j\) for CITs, competitor for RITs), one array per split.

null_values_ list of ndarray or None

Null distribution of the test statistic for each split (None when null_dist is "normality").

Name Type Description self object

docs.title: summarize(cross_fit=None, combine=None, reverse=False, verbose=True)
docs.text:
Summarize inference results

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cross_fit bool

If True, inference results will be integrated across folds by cross-fitting strategy. It is applicable only if learner is a Crosser with n_folds > 1. If applicable, None means True; Otherwise, None means False.

None combine bool

If True, inference results will be combined across folds and repeats. For estimates and std_error, simple average is used for combination. For p_value, the following p-value combination methods are reported (with \(m\) p-values and order statistics \(p_{(1)} \le ... \le p_{(m)}\)):

- "gmean": $e$ times the geometric mean.
- "median": twice the median.
- "min": $m p_{(1)}$ (Bonferroni).
- "hmean": $e \log(m)$ times the harmonic mean.
- "hommel": Hommel's combination.
- "cauchy": Cauchy combination test.

It is applicable only if learner is a Crosser with n_splits > 1. If n_repeats > 1, None means True; Otherwise, None means False.

None reverse bool

If True, negative values of estimate will be reported.

False verbose bool

Controls the verbosity.

True

Returns:

Name Type Description summary DataFrame

A summary for inference results.

docs.title: Cross-fitting
docs.text:
Bases: BaseEstimator

An object for repeated cross-fitting

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default estimator estimator object

The base estimator for repeated cross-fitting.

required cv cross-validation generator

The cross-validation generator for repeated cross-fitting. It must be a class member of KFold, RepeatedKFold, or ShuffleSplit. Its random_state must be an int (or None for KFold without shuffling) so that every call to split yields the same folds.

required scoring str or callable

Strategy to evaluate the performance of the cross-validated model when using summarize. To see availble scoring methods via str, use sklearn.get_scorer_names().

- For regression tasks, `None` means "r2".
- For classification tasks, `None` means "accuracy".
None

Attributes:

Name Type Description estimators_ list of estimators

The fitted estimators, one per split.

classes_ list

Class labels (classifiers only).

label_binarizer_ LabelBinarizer

Binarizer fitted on all class labels (classifiers only).

val_scores_, train_scores_, test_scores_ ndarray of shape (n_splits,)

Validation (best_score_ of the estimator, if any), training and test scores of each split.

docs.title: summarize(cross_fit=None, combine=None, reverse=False, verbose=True)
docs.text:
Summarize repeated cross-fitting results

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cross_fit bool

If True, score values will be averaged across folds. It is applicable if n_folds > 1. If applicable, None means True; Otherwise, None means False.

None combine bool

If True, score values will be averaged across folds and repeats. It is applicable if n_splits > 1. If n_repeats > 1, None means True; Otherwise, None means False.

None reverse bool

If True, negative score values will be reported. Note that by default a larger score value means better in scikit-learn.

False verbose bool

Controls the verbosity.

True

Returns:

Name Type Description summary DataFrame

A summary for validation, train, and test scores (val_score, train_score, and test_score). The validation scores are only presented if estimator.best_score_ is available.

docs.title: predict(X, *, split=None)
docs.text:
Predict with one split's estimator, or aggregate all splits.

With split=None, regression predictions are averaged and classification predictions are combined by majority vote (ties go to the smallest label).

docs.title: Warnings and errors
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Warning raised when the inference setup may leak test information.

It is emitted when learner is a Crosser but sampler (CIT) or competitor (RIT) is an ordinary estimator. If that estimator was fitted on data that includes the test folds of learner, the resulting test is invalid. Use warnings.simplefilter("error", LeakageWarning) to turn it into an error.

Bases: ValueError

Exception raised if an inferer is summarized before infer.

Bases: ValueError, TypeError

Exception raised for an invalid argument.

It subclasses both ValueError and TypeError (as scikit-learn's InvalidParameterError does), so code written against tofi 0.0.1, which raised ValueError for every invalid argument, keeps working.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• zero_one_loss returned 1 for correct predictions, so tests based on it were reversed. It now returns 1 for errors.
  • CIT evaluated the resampled data with predict instead of predict_proba, giving wrong losses for classifiers with log_loss.
  • CIT with a plain (non-Crosser) binary classifier compared a one-column target with two-column probabilities under log_loss.
  • Crosser failed with scikit-learn >= 1.8 because _estimator_type was removed. It now implements __sklearn_tags__ (and keeps _estimator_type for older versions).
  • Installing from GitHub failed because pyproject.toml had no [build-system] and package configuration.
  • Two separately created but identical cross-validators (e.g. KFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=0)) were rejected as different.

docs.title: Behaviour changes
docs.text:
• RIT now defaults to method="LOCO" (previously documented as "PIE"), following Huang (2025). method is now optional for both CIT (default "RPT") and RIT.
  • PIE's double splitting now divides each test set into two random halves instead of odd/even rows. A UserWarning is issued when double splitting is used with random_state=None, because the results then cannot be replicated.
  • Each fold and each source of randomness (sampling, permutation, perturbation, double splitting) now receives an independent seed derived from random_state. Results for a given random_state therefore differ from 0.0.1.
  • The combined p-value "q1" (the second smallest p-value times \(m/2\)) is removed from the summarize(combine=True) output.
  • RIT with null_dist="resampling" now raises an error instead of warning and failing later.
  • Crosser rejects a cv whose random_state is a RandomState instance, which would produce different folds on each call.
  • infer returns self.
  • The arguments of CIT, RIT and Crosser are no longer overwritten with their defaults. The settings actually used are available as method_, loss_func_, null_dist_, double_split_, n_copies_ and n_permutations_ (e.g. RIT(...).method is now None when not given, and RIT(...).method_ is "LOCO").
  • Invalid arguments raise InvalidParameterError, which subclasses both ValueError (as in 0.0.1) and TypeError.
  • Permutation null distributions are generated in vectorized blocks. They have the same distribution as before, but a given random_state yields different permutations (and hence slightly different permutation p-values) than earlier development versions.

docs.title: Other changes
docs.text:
• LeakageWarning when learner is a Crosser but sampler/competitor is an ordinary estimator.
  • Crosser is now a scikit-learn BaseEstimator (supports get_params, clone and repr).
  • Crosser.predict (majority vote over splits) now works with non-integer class labels.
  • Internal refactoring: one code path for Crosser and ordinary estimators, shared null-distribution helpers, consistent formatting (ruff).
  • Tests (176): unit tests, statistical checks of the null distributions against their exact moments, and regression tests that lock the numerical results of 48 scenarios (tests/golden). GitHub Actions CI with linting, and an API documentation site.
• Initial release.
